records.real_world_identity_notes: Mid-engined racing version of the M1 built for the one-make Procar series that supported Formula One in 1979 and 1980. It keeps the road car's ZF five-speed, whose first gear sits on a dogleg so that first, third and fifth share the lower plane, with revised ratios and an added oil cooler for racing.

records.specification_basis: The sources establish a ZF five-speed with a dogleg first gear, and the live drive confirmed five gears through an H-pattern gate observed as a dogleg.

The dogleg gate was seen directly in the cockpit during the guided drive and is independently corroborated by the registered sources. First gear sits out of the racing shift plane, so second through fifth fall in one straight sequence.

additional_claims.basis: The guided drive recorded that the upshift was accepted after a throttle lift and the downshift after the driver's manual blip, with no automatic cut or blip detected.

records.real_world_identity_notes: Reiza's fictionalised take on the Australian Supercars category. The real championship runs an Albins six-speed sequential transaxle, a 1100 Nm unit developed for the Next Generation cars in 2012 that integrates gearbox, differential and drive-axle components, and the championship confirmed for Gen3 that the manual stick-shift mechanism is retained rather than moving to paddles. That is why this car is shifted by a lever where a modern GT would use paddles. The dataset does not claim the AMS2 labels are an exact identity match for any specific entrant.
records.confidence_basis: Simulator behavior was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the category's six-speed sequential transaxle and retained stick shift are established by the championship and the transmission manufacturer.
records.identity_basis: The championship and transmission manufacturer establish the category architecture, and the exact simulator identity was observed live. The car is a fictionalised representation rather than a named entrant.
records.specification_basis: The category uses an Albins six-speed sequential transaxle with a retained manual stick shift, and the live drive confirmed six gears through a sequential lever with the clutch required to move off.
control_notes: Simulator behavior was directly observed in a guided drive with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.
The category deliberately retains a manual stick shift on a six-speed sequential transaxle, so the car is shifted by a lever rather than paddles.

No throttle lift is required on upshifts because a full-throttle clutchless upshift was accepted with automatic cut detected. No automatic blip was detected, so the driver supplies the downshift blip, matching the curated convention for a sequential stick without automatic blip.
